why.title: And that’s not all.
why.lead: Six more reasons. Follow the thread down the page.

r1.title: Your voice stays home
r1.text: Dictation and voice mode are transcribed by your own computer. Elsewhere, your voice is often sent off to a server.

r2.title: Nothing to set up
r2.text: Install the app, open it: no server to start, no container. The engine that runs the models is included, and so is the image engine. Already have models in Ollama? ChatonLM brings them over in one click, without downloading them again.

r3.title: It knows your machine
r3.text: ModelHub reads your graphics card and memory, then points you to the models, for text or images, that fit your machine. No more 20 GB downloads for nothing.

r4.title: Linux doesn’t wait its turn
r4.text: The same tools on Linux and on Windows. Many AI apps stop at Windows and macOS.

r5.title: The code is open
r5.text: ChatonLM is open-source software under the MIT license. Anyone can read what the app does, change it, and check that it hides nothing.

r6.title: It speaks your language
r6.text: Interface in English, French and Spanish, natural voices in all three languages, dictation in 99. ChatonLM is designed in France.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.a1: Yes. ChatonLM is open-source software under the MIT license: no paid version, no subscription, no ads. The open models you download are free too.
faq.q2: Do I need a graphics card?
faq.a2: No. Models also run on the processor, just more slowly. With a graphics card they run faster and can be bigger; ModelHub tells you which ones fit your machine. For images, a graphics card makes all the difference: on the processor, expect several minutes per image.
faq.q3: Is it as capable as the big online AIs?
faq.a3: Not at everything. A model that fits on your computer is smaller than the ones behind the big online services. For chatting, summarizing, proofreading, translating, studying or dictating, it does the job very well, and your data stays with you.
faq.a4: Not for now. ChatonLM is available for Windows 11 and Linux, 64-bit.
faq.q5: What else do I need to install?
faq.a5: Nothing to get started. The engine that runs the models is included; you just pick a model in ModelHub, and one click is enough. Voices and speech recognition are downloaded the first time you use them.
faq.q6: Windows shows a warning during installation
faq.a6: ChatonLM is a young app: its installer doesn’t yet have a certificate that Windows recognizes, hence the “Windows protected your PC” screen. Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. The code is open, and every update is signed.
faq.what_a: ChatonLM is a free, open-source local AI app for Windows 11 and Linux. It brings seven tools together in one window: chat with a language model (LLM), a model catalog, voice dictation, voice (read aloud and voice mode), proofreading, study and image generation. Models run on your own computer, with no account and no subscription.
faq.offline_q: Does it work without an internet connection?
faq.offline_a: Yes, once your models, voices and speech recognition are downloaded. Chat, image generation, dictation, voice, proofreading and study all work offline. The internet is only used to browse the catalog, to download models and voices, to check for updates and, if you turn them on, for web search, remote models and Easy Link.
faq.models_a: Models you can download and run locally, such as Gemma, Qwen, Mistral or Llama. ModelHub lists them in one catalog, tells you which ones fit your machine, and installs them in one click.
faq.images_a: Yes, in the chat: describe the picture, and the built-in image engine draws it on your computer, with an open model chosen in ModelHub. With a graphics card, an image takes from a few seconds to about a minute with the recommended models, longer with the heaviest ones or on a modest card; on the processor, several minutes. All about image generation
faq.engine_q: Do I need Ollama to use ChatonLM?
faq.engine_a: No. ChatonLM has its own engine, built on llama.cpp, and downloads its models from Hugging Face. If you already use Ollama, ChatonLM copies your models in one click, without downloading them again, and leaves your Ollama as it is. ChatonLM is an independent project: it is not affiliated with Ollama, nor endorsed by it.
faq.vscode_q: Does ChatonLM work with VS Code?
faq.vscode_a: Yes, with the ChatonLM extension for VS Code (and VSCodium): it explains, fixes and completes your code with your local models, and gives you spoken tours of it. All about the extension

end.lead: All that’s left is to adopt it.

legal.title: Legal notice
legal.lead: Who publishes this site, who hosts it, and under which license ChatonLM is released.
legal.body:
Publisher

The chatonlm.com website is published by a private individual, in a non-professional capacity. As permitted by article 1-1, II of French Act No. 2004-575 of 21 June 2004 on confidence in the digital economy, the publisher’s identity has been provided to the site’s hosting provider.

Contact: contact.chatonlm@gmail.com, or the contact form.

Hosting provider

OVH SAS, 2 rue Kellermann, 59100 Roubaix, France. Phone: 1007. Website: ovhcloud.com.

Software license

ChatonLM is open-source software, released under the MIT license. It builds on open-source software and open models, including llama.cpp, whose engine it bundles; their licenses come with every version of the app. Its interface adapts parts of the Ollama app, also under the MIT license.

ChatonLM is neither affiliated with Ollama nor endorsed by it. “Ollama” is a trademark of its owner, mentioned here to describe where the interface comes from and the import of its models.

Site content

The texts and drawings on this site, including the kitten, belong to their author. The Fraunces, Figtree and Unbounded fonts are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

Links

The files available for download are hosted by GitHub. This site is not responsible for the content of the sites it links to.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: This site doesn’t track you: no cookies, no analytics, no content loaded from a third party.
privacy.body:
When you visit this site

No cookie is set and no analytics tool is installed. The fonts and images come from the site itself.

Like any web server, ours records the IP address, the date, the requested page, the browser used and the referring page in a technical log. This log is used for the security and proper running of the site; it is deleted automatically after a few weeks.

When you write to us

The form sends us your name, your email address and your message by email, to a Gmail (Google) mailbox. They are used only to reply to you and are not stored anywhere else. The controller of this processing is the site’s publisher, relying on its legitimate interest in replying to you. Google may store these emails outside the European Union. They are deleted at the latest one year after our last exchange.

To limit abusive submissions, your IP address is kept in working memory for one day at most, never on disk.

When you download ChatonLM

The files are hosted by GitHub: your browser downloads them from GitHub, which therefore sees your IP address, under its own privacy policy.

In the ChatonLM app

ChatonLM has no account, no telemetry and no analytics. Your conversations, attachments, the images you create and your settings stay on your computer; dictation and voice mode are transcribed locally, and images are made there too. The text that dictation and proofreading put on the clipboard stays out of its history and, on Windows, out of its cloud sync.

An ephemeral chat, opened with the ghost kitten, stays out of your history: it is erased, down to the database files, as soon as you open another chat or quit the app, unless you choose to keep it.

The app only connects to:

  • Hugging Face, when you open ModelHub (model lists and model pages, image models included), when you download a model, an image model, a speech recognition model or a voice, and to check whether a model installed from Hugging Face has a newer version;
  • GitHub, to check for and download updates, and to download the files of a voice;
  • ChatonLM’s search service (relay.chatonlm.com), only when a model searches the web: it receives the search and returns results from Brave Search. There is no account: your installation registers once with a key of its own, made on your computer. Only the titles and links of the results are kept with the conversation (details: Web search);
  • GitHub and NVIDIA, only if you ask for NVIDIA acceleration, to download its pack: ChatonLM’s part from GitHub, NVIDIA’s libraries from NVIDIA, under its license, shown first;
  • the providers of remote models you add with your own API key, only if you turn remote models on (they are off by default);
  • Telegram or Discord, only if you connect a bot with Easy Link (see below).
  • chatonlm.com, only when you send a bug report from the settings (see below).

Conversations with a local model are handled by the engine built into ChatonLM, on your computer. Remote models are off by default: if you turn them on in the settings and pick one, your messages and their attachments are sent to its provider and processed on its servers, under its own terms. Dictation is never sent to a remote model.

When you create an image

The image is made on your computer by the image engine built into ChatonLM (stable-diffusion.cpp), which runs locally and does not connect to the internet. Your description and the image stay on your computer; the image is saved with the conversation and is never sent back to the language model. When the language model is the one asking for the image, your message goes to that model, like any message.

With Easy Link

Easy Link lets you write to your models from Telegram or Discord, through a bot you create yourself. As long as you haven’t connected a bot, the app doesn’t connect to either service. Once a bot is connected, and while the app is running, your messages to the bot (text, photos, voice messages) and everything it replies, the model’s answers and the images it creates included, go through the servers of that service, under its own privacy policy. The app talks to that service directly: no other server sits in between, and nothing is sent to ChatonLM’s publisher.

The bot’s token is kept in the app’s database, on your computer, and is only sent to that service. Voice messages are transcribed on your computer, the model answers as it does in the app, and these conversations are saved on your computer with the others, except in ephemeral mode (the /ephemeral on command), where they are erased as in the app.

With the VS Code extension

The ChatonLM extension for VS Code connects to the app through a link that stays on your computer (a local channel that does not go through the network). The link is off until you allow it, and only editors paired with a code can use it. The code, changes or terminal output you attach to a request go to the model chosen in ChatonLM, like any message: with a local model, they stay on your computer. Before each request, the panel shows what is sent; to a remote model, it leaves out sensitive files (such as .env files or keys) and masks, as best it can, lines that look like secrets. The extension can only read and continue the chats started in the editor: those of the app and of your bots stay closed to it.

The extension has no telemetry. Easy Link notifications only contain the task’s name, how long it took and whether it worked, never code or terminal output. The editor’s agents, if you give them access, see neither your chats nor your settings. The extension is installed from Microsoft’s Visual Studio Marketplace or from Open VSX (Eclipse Foundation), under their own privacy policies.

When you report a bug

From Settings › General, “Report a bug” sends your message to chatonlm.com, which forwards it to us by email, to the same Gmail inbox as the website form. Nothing is sent until you click Send. You can leave an email address so we can reply, or not.

If you leave the diagnostic box ticked, it goes with your message: versions of ChatonLM and of its engine (llama.cpp, with the graphics card it uses), system, type of installation and the end of the app’s technical log. You can read it before sending. It never contains your conversations; your home folder and user name are hidden. These messages are kept and deleted like those of the form, and your IP address is used in the same way to limit abuse.

The app’s technical log (the chatonlm.log file) stays on your computer; only what you send reaches us.

Your rights

You can ask to see, correct or delete the data about you, or object to its processing, by writing to contact.chatonlm@gmail.com. You can also lodge a complaint with the CNIL (cnil.fr).

search.title: Web search
search.lead: Terms and privacy of ChatonLM’s search service: free, without an account, and without any log of your searches.
search.body:
The service

When a model searches the web in ChatonLM, the app goes through ChatonLM’s search service (relay.chatonlm.com). This free service, with no account, passes the search on to a partner search engine, currently Brave Search (with Mojeek as a fallback), and returns the titles, links and short snippets of the results to the app. Its code is public, in the ChatonLM repository: everything below can be checked there.

Terms of use

By using ChatonLM’s web search, you agree to these rules:

  • the service is for the searches of a person chatting with a model in ChatonLM; querying it from another program, automating it at scale or getting around its limits (multiplied installations, forged keys) is forbidden;
  • results are for the current conversation: they may not be resold, redistributed, gathered into a database, or used to train or evaluate an artificial intelligence model;
  • these rules follow the ones Brave sets for the users of applications built on its API, and Brave’s results remain subject to its own terms; the app shows with the results that they are provided by Brave Search;
  • each installation gets 50 searches a day; the service has a monthly budget, paid for by donations: once it is reached, search is paused until the next month, and an overly busy day can pause it until the next day;
  • the service is provided as is, with no guarantee of availability, nor of accuracy or completeness of the results, which come from third parties; it may be paused, limited or stopped at any time, and an installation that breaks these rules may be excluded from it.

Privacy

What the service keeps. The public key of each installation, made by the app on your computer at the first search: a pseudonymous identifier, not linked to your name, an email address or your IP address, kept with the day it registered and the day it was last used, and deleted after 90 days without a search. To keep to its budget, the service also keeps monthly and daily totals (searches per engine, spending), with nothing about you in them.

What it never keeps. Neither your IP address, nor the text of your searches, nor the results. No search is written to a log, and the web server keeps no access log for this service.

In memory only. To limit abuse, the service counts searches per installation and per network (your IP address reduced to the network that contains it); these counters are never written to disk and start again from zero every day. This processing is based on the publisher’s legitimate interest in protecting the service. If a serious failure hits the web server, its error log may record the IP address of the connection involved; it is deleted after two weeks.

What the search engine sees. Brave (or Mojeek) receives the text of the search, its language and its country, from ChatonLM’s server: not your IP address, your key or your identity. Brave, based in the United States, and Mojeek, based in the United Kingdom, keep searches for up to 90 days, tied to ChatonLM’s account, under their own privacy policies.

In the app. Of the results, only the titles and links are kept with the conversation, on your computer. When a model reads a page it found, the app opens it directly from your computer: the site visited then sees your IP address, as it would with a browser.

The controller for this processing is the publisher of the website (see the legal notice); you can exercise your rights as described on the Privacy page.

dictation.eyebrow: Offline voice dictation · Windows and Linux
dictation.title: You talk, it types.
dictation.lead: ChatonLM’s dictation turns your voice into text, on your own computer. Press a shortcut, speak in any app, and the text appears where your cursor is. Nothing goes online.
dictation.step1_text: Wherever you are: in an email, a document, a chat. Ctrl+Alt+D by default, and you can change it.
dictation.step2_text: Normally, at your own pace. ChatonLM recognizes speech on your computer; a model can then restore punctuation and remove hesitations.
dictation.step3_text: It is pasted where your cursor is, and stays in the clipboard. A setting lets you just copy it instead.
dictation.fact1_text: Two engines to choose from: Parakeet, fast, for 25 European languages, which detects the spoken language on its own; Whisper, for 99 languages.
dictation.fact2_text: A personal dictionary keeps the spelling of names and of the terms of your trade.
dictation.fact3_text: If you want, a local model tidies the transcript: punctuation, filler words, self-corrections. You set its instructions.
dictation.fact4_text: Press once to start and once to stop, or hold the key while you speak.
dictation.fact5_text: Speech recognition runs on the processor. Whisper needs a processor with AVX2; Parakeet works on any 64-bit PC.
dictation.fact6_text: The shortcut is global: it answers over your browser, your mail, your word processor.
dictation.privacy_text: Many dictation services send your voice to a server to transcribe it. Here, the recording never leaves your computer: recognition happens on the spot, and nothing is kept online. Even the tidying of the text is done by a model on your computer: dictation never uses a remote model.
dictation.q1: Does dictation work without the internet?
dictation.a1: Yes. Once the speech recognition model is downloaded, the first time you use it, everything happens on your computer, even offline.
dictation.q2: Which languages can I dictate in?
dictation.a2: 99 languages with Whisper, including English, French and Spanish. Parakeet covers 25 European languages and recognizes on its own the one you speak.
dictation.q3: Does it work in every app?
dictation.a3: Yes: the shortcut is global, and the text is pasted where your cursor is. On Windows, you choose the shortcut in the settings. On Linux, it goes through KDE Plasma 6 or GNOME 48 and later; on another desktop, you bind a command to the key you want. On Linux, the desktop asks for your permission the first time ChatonLM pastes; if it doesn’t allow it, the text stays copied, ready to paste.
dictation.q4: Do I need a powerful computer?
dictation.a4: No. Recognition runs on the processor, with no graphics card. Whisper needs a recent processor (AVX2); Parakeet works on any 64-bit PC.
dictation.a5: Yes. Dictation is part of ChatonLM, open-source software under the MIT license: no subscription, no account.

chat.eyebrow: Local AI chat · Windows and Linux
chat.title: Ask away, at home.
chat.lead: ChatonLM’s chat lets you talk with a language model that runs on your own computer. You type, it answers, and nothing you say goes off to an online service.
chat.step1_text: ModelHub shows you the ones that fit your machine and installs them in one click.
chat.step2_text: A question, a text to summarize, a snippet of code. Add an image or a PDF if the subject calls for it.
chat.step3_text: It’s written out before your eyes, formatted as it goes: headings, tables, highlighted code, formulas.
chat.fact1_text: Drop a file into the window: images for models that can see, PDFs, text and code files.
chat.fact2_text: Reasoning models get their own Think button, with a thinking level when the model allows it.
chat.fact3_text: Your conversations are kept on your computer, with favorites. Every message can still be edited. Long conversations are compacted, automatically or on demand, to fit in the model’s memory.
chat.fact4_text: The ghost kitten opens an ephemeral chat: it stays out of your history and is erased as soon as you move to another chat or quit the app, unless you keep it.
chat.fact5_title: The web, if you want it
chat.fact5_text: Turn on web search, and the model can look things up online, with no account. It’s optional: turned off, nothing goes out.
chat.fact6_text: Keep a model in memory for as long as you like, or load it when the app opens so the first answer doesn’t have to wait. Quit the app, and the memory is freed.
chat.privacy_text: Online AI services receive everything you write to them. Here, the model runs on your computer: your messages, attachments and history never leave it. Two exceptions, which are yours to decide: web search, which sends the model’s searches to ChatonLM’s search service; and a remote model, if you turn remote models on and pick one: your messages then go to its provider.
chat.q1: Does it work without the internet?
chat.a1: Yes, once the model is downloaded. The chat happens entirely on your computer.
chat.q2: Do I need a graphics card?
chat.a2: No. Models also run on the processor, just more slowly. With a graphics card they answer faster and can be bigger.
chat.a3: Models you can download and run locally, such as Gemma, Qwen, Mistral or Llama. ModelHub tells you which ones fit your machine.
chat.q4: Is it as capable as the big online AIs?
chat.a4: Not at everything. A model that fits on your computer is smaller than the ones behind the big online services. For chatting, summarizing, proofreading, translating or studying, it does the job very well, and your data stays with you. To go further, remote models are available as an option, off by default: with your own API key from a provider (Ollama Cloud, OpenRouter, Mistral, or any server compatible with the OpenAI API), they run on its servers.
chat.q5: Do I need to create an account?
chat.a5: No. ChatonLM has no account and no subscription, and web search doesn’t need one either. Only remote models, if you want them, need an API key from their provider.

hub.eyebrow: Local AI models · Hugging Face catalog
hub.title: The right model, on the first try.
hub.lead: ModelHub is ChatonLM’s model catalog. It reads your graphics card and memory, browses the open models on Hugging Face and tells you which ones fit your machine, before you download anything.
hub.step1_text: The models of the moment, which you can filter by size, capabilities, license or verified publisher.
hub.step2_text: Each version says whether it fits your graphics card, fits in memory, or is too large.
hub.step3_text: One click, and the model downloads. It shows up in chat as soon as it’s ready.
hub.fact1_text: ModelHub reads your graphics card and memory. No more 20 GB downloads for nothing.
hub.fact2_text: Fits your GPU, fits in memory, runs partly on CPU, or too large.
hub.fact3_text: “Fits my machine”, size, capabilities, open license, verified publishers only.
hub.fact4_text: Its author’s description, its license and its versions, without leaving the app.
hub.fact5_text: The progress of every download in one tab, and your installed models in another.
hub.fact6_text: Image models, speech recognition models and read-aloud voices are chosen in the same place.
hub.privacy_text: To show the catalog and download a model, ChatonLM connects to Hugging Face: that’s the only time ModelHub goes online. No account is required, and your machine is examined locally: nothing ModelHub learns about your graphics card or memory is sent anywhere.
hub.q1: Where do the models come from?
hub.a1: From Hugging Face, the largest library of open models. ModelHub shows its compatible models (GGUF files) and installs them for the engine included in ChatonLM; image models run in its image engine. Models you already have in Ollama can be imported in one click, without downloading them again.
hub.q2: How do I know whether a model will run on my machine?
hub.a2: ModelHub compares the size of each version with your graphics card and memory, then shows the result on a label. The “Fits my machine” filter keeps only the ones that fit.
hub.q3: Do I need a Hugging Face account?
hub.a3: No. ChatonLM doesn’t ask for any account to browse the catalog or to download.
hub.a4: Yes: they’re open models, free to download. Each has its own license, shown on its model card; a filter keeps only open licenses.
hub.a5: On your computer, in ChatonLM’s data: language models in one folder, image models in another. For the former, you can choose another folder in the settings, for example on a bigger drive, and ChatonLM can move your models there.

voice.eyebrow: Voice mode and read aloud · runs locally
voice.title: Talk to it, it talks back.
voice.lead: ChatonLM’s voice does two things: it reads answers aloud in a natural voice, and it holds a hands-free conversation. You speak, the model answers out loud, then listens again. It all happens on your computer.
voice.step1_text: The waveform button, next to Send, or Ctrl+Shift+Space.
voice.step2_text: ChatonLM sends your sentence when you pause. Prefer to stay in control? Hold Space while you speak.
voice.step3_text: The answer is read aloud. To interrupt it, just speak: ChatonLM goes quiet and listens.
voice.fact1_text: One voice per language, in English, French and Spanish, downloaded once.
voice.fact2_text: Any answer can be read aloud, in one click or automatically, while it’s being written. In other apps, a shortcut reads the text you selected.
voice.fact3_text: ChatonLM removes its own voice from what the microphone hears: you interrupt it by speaking, even on speakers.
voice.fact4_text: Let ChatonLM spot your pauses, or hold Space while you speak.
voice.fact5_text: In voice mode, the model is instructed to keep its answers short, the way people talk. You can change that instruction.
voice.fact6_text: The conversation is displayed and saved as usual: you’ll find it in your history.
voice.privacy_text: Speech detection, transcription, echo cancellation and the voice all run on your computer. Only the transcribed text is sent to the model, like a message typed on the keyboard, and with a local model it stays on your machine. With a remote model, if you pick one, that text is processed by its provider.
voice.q1: Does voice mode work without the internet?
voice.a1: Yes, once the voice and the speech recognition model are downloaded. ChatonLM offers to download them the first time, and tells you their size.
voice.a2: Answers are read aloud in English, French and Spanish, with the voice of their language. An answer in another language is written, not read.
voice.a3: No. Echo cancellation lets you interrupt an answer by speaking, even with speakers. With headphones, it’s cleaner still.
voice.q4: Can I just have answers read aloud?
voice.a4: Yes. Without voice mode, a button under each answer reads it aloud, and a setting reads new answers automatically. Anywhere else, select some text and press the read-aloud shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+R suggested, turned on in Settings › Keyboard shortcuts): ChatonLM reads it, and pressing again stops it.
voice.q5: What do I need to get started?
voice.a5: A microphone, the voice for your language and a speech recognition model. When one is missing, ChatonLM offers to download it, then starts.

proofread.title: Your mistakes, fixed at home.
proofread.lead: ChatonLM’s proofreading checks your writing with a model that runs on your own computer. It corrects mistakes or rephrases, in the language of the text and without changing its meaning. Nothing is sent online.
proofread.step1_text: Into the app’s Proofread page. Or select it wherever you’re writing, and press the shortcut.
proofread.step2_text: “Correct” only touches the mistakes. “Rephrase” also improves the sentences.
proofread.step3_text: Every change is highlighted: what was removed, what was added. One click is enough to undo.
proofread.fact1_text: A global shortcut corrects the selected text and pastes the result in its place.
proofread.fact2_text: Two buttons, two purposes: fix the mistakes, or rewrite more clearly.
proofread.fact3_text: The corrected text replaces yours, with deletions and additions highlighted, and the number of corrections.
proofread.fact4_title: In the language of the text
proofread.fact4_text: The text keeps its language and its meaning: proofreading doesn’t translate and doesn’t make anything up. Options also keep the words in their order, the formatting, or numbers as digits.
proofread.fact5_text: On “Auto”, proofreading uses the largest model already loaded, or else the chat model. Or pick one, once and for all.
proofread.fact6_text: A long text is corrected part by part, and you can stop along the way.
proofread.privacy_text: An online proofreader reads everything you hand it: letters, reports, messages. Here, the proofreading is done by a model installed on your computer, and your texts never leave it. One exception, which is yours to decide: a remote model, if you turn them on and proofreading uses one.
proofread.q1: Does proofreading work without the internet?
proofread.a1: Yes, once the model is downloaded. The text is checked on your computer.
proofread.a2: In the languages the chosen model knows: English, French and Spanish with most models, and many more with the largest ones.
proofread.q3: What’s the difference between correcting and rephrasing?
proofread.a3: Correcting fixes spelling, grammar and punctuation, without touching your sentences. Rephrasing also rewrites awkward wording, while keeping the meaning.
proofread.q4: Does the shortcut replace my text on its own?
proofread.a4: Yes, by default: the corrected text is pasted over the selection. A setting turns this off: the result is then only copied, and you paste it with Ctrl+V. On Linux, your desktop asks for your permission the first time.
proofread.a5: A medium-sized model proofreads better than a very small one. ModelHub shows you the ones that fit your machine.

study.eyebrow: Learn with a local AI · courses and quizzes
study.title: One topic, one tailor-made course.
study.lead: ChatonLM’s Study tool turns any topic into a course. Your model writes the lessons, examples and quizzes, level by level, and you only move on once you’ve got it. All on your computer.
study.step1_text: Photosynthesis, Python lists, the French Revolution. Add your documents if the course should stick to them.
study.step2_text: “Discover”, “I know the basics” or “Go deeper”, and how much time you want to spend.
study.step3_text: A lesson, some examples, then a quiz. Pass it, and you move on to the next. Miss it, and the tutor explains it another way.
study.fact1_text: Science, languages, history, programming: the course takes the shape that suits the topic.
study.fact2_text: Attach a PDF or a text file: the course builds on it. Web search can add to it, if you’ve turned it on.
study.fact3_text: Three starting points, no placement test, and a duration of your choice.
study.fact4_text: Each level is passed by answering questions. If you slip up: an explanation of where it went wrong, then new questions.
study.fact5_text: Something still unclear? Ask the tutor, without leaving the lesson.
study.fact6_text: Completed courses stay in the Study tab: you can reread them whenever you like.
study.privacy_text: Your topics, documents and answers never leave your computer: it’s your own model that writes the course. Two exceptions, which are yours to decide: web search, if you turn it on, sends the model’s searches to ChatonLM’s search service; and a remote model, if study uses one, receives what the model reads.
study.q1: What topics can I create a course on?
study.a1: Any topic: a concept in biology, a grammar rule, a chapter of history, a programming language. The more specific the topic, the better the course.
study.a2: A model can get things wrong, especially a small one. A larger model writes better lessons (on “Auto”, ChatonLM uses the largest one already loaded), and a course based on your documents sticks to them more closely. For an exam, check against your own materials.
study.q3: How long does a course take?
study.a3: As long as you choose: about twenty minutes is a good benchmark, more or less depending on what you want to learn.
study.q4: Can I study from my own course materials?
study.a4: Yes. Attach your documents when you create the course: the lessons and quizzes are drawn from them.
study.q5: Does it work without the internet?
study.a5: Yes, once the model is downloaded. Only web search, which is optional, needs a connection.

images.title: Your pictures, drawn at home.
images.lead: ChatonLM creates images from a description, right in the chat. The image engine is built in and runs on your computer: your description and the picture stay with you. And you choose the model, from open models.
images.step1_text: In ModelHub, Images tab: each model says what it’s good at, how long it takes and whether it fits your graphics card. Download it, then click Use.
images.step2_text: In a chat, turn on the Image button and write what you want to see: the subject, the style, the colors, the light.
images.step3_text: The picture sharpens step by step before your eyes, then appears in the chat. A button lets you save it.
images.fact1_text: No separate program: the picture lands in the chat, next to your messages, and stays in your history.
images.fact2_text: The Image button sends your text as is to the image model. Or simply ask a model that can use tools for a picture: it writes a detailed description itself.
images.fact3_text: FLUX.2 klein, Z-Image, FLUX.1, Stable Diffusion XL and more: ModelHub shows the open models on Hugging Face from the families ChatonLM recognizes, not a handful of models picked in advance.
images.fact4_text: What it’s good at, how long an image takes, how much graphics memory it needs, and what its license allows: free use, non-commercial use, or a license to read.
images.fact5_title: With or without a graphics card
images.fact5_text: A graphics card does the heavy lifting. Without one, the processor takes over, at several minutes per image, and ChatonLM tells you beforehand.
images.fact6_title: All the way to your phone
images.fact6_text: With Easy Link, ask your Telegram or Discord bot for a picture: if its model can use tools and an image model is chosen in ChatonLM, the image arrives as a photo.
images.privacy_text: An online image generator receives every description you write and makes the picture on its servers. Here, the image engine runs on your computer: your descriptions and pictures never leave it. The internet is only used to browse image models and download them from Hugging Face. Two exceptions, which are yours to decide: with Easy Link, pictures go through your messaging service; and a remote model, if you pick one, receives your messages, but never the pictures it creates.
images.q1: Do I need a graphics card?
images.a1: It’s strongly recommended. With a graphics card, an image takes from a few seconds to about a minute with the recommended models, longer with the heaviest ones or on a modest card. Without one, the processor does the work, at several minutes per image. The image engine also needs a recent processor (with AVX2).
images.q2: How long does an image take?
images.a2: It depends on the model and your machine. ModelHub shows it for each model: an estimate at first, then the time measured on your computer from your first image on. The fastest ones, such as FLUX.2 klein 4B, take a few seconds on a powerful graphics card. The first image after a break, or after switching models, takes longer: the model is loading.
images.q3: Where do the models come from, and under what license?
images.a3: From Hugging Face, the big library of open models; they download with no account. Each model has its own license, and ModelHub spells it out: free use, non-commercial use, or a license to read. The two recommended models, FLUX.2 klein 4B and Z-Image-Turbo, are under the Apache 2.0 license: free use.
images.a4: No: your description and the picture are processed on your computer, by the built-in image engine. Only the list of models and their downloads go over the internet. With Easy Link, the picture is sent to your bot, since that’s where you asked for it. And if you pick a remote model, your messages are sent to its provider, but never the pictures it creates.
images.a5: Yes. Image generation is part of ChatonLM, open-source software under the MIT license: no credits to buy, no subscription, no account. The models are free to download; their license says what you may do with the pictures.

vscode.title: Your models, in your editor.
vscode.lead: The ChatonLM extension for VS Code puts the models on your computer to work on your code: explain it, fix it, write tests, complete as you type, even talk it through out loud. It relies on the ChatonLM app on the same machine: no account, no subscription, no API key.
vscode.requires: You also need the ChatonLM app, version 0.9.4 or later, on the same computer. Download ChatonLM
vscode.demo_q: Why cut at the last dash?
vscode.demo_a: So a word is never cut in half: when the title is too long, the slug keeps what comes before the last dash, whole words only. With no dash, it cuts at the limit.
vscode.step1_text: Download the app for Windows or Linux and choose a model. The app runs the models; the extension goes through it.
vscode.step2_text: Search for “ChatonLM” in the VS Code extensions. VSCodium, Cursor and the other editors that rely on Open VSX find it there.
vscode.step3_text: In ChatonLM, open Settings, VS Code tab: allow VS Code to connect, then choose Pair an editor. Type the code it shows in the ChatonLM panel of VS Code.
vscode.fact1_text: Select some code, then Explain, Fix or Write Tests, or ask your own question. It also writes your commit messages. Before anything is sent, the panel shows what goes to the model.
vscode.fact2_text: A guided tour reads a file or your changes part by part, highlighting the part being read. Talk your code through hands-free, or dictate at the cursor: voices and speech recognition run on your computer.
vscode.fact3_text: Off by default. A small code model suggests what comes next, in grey. ChatonLM loads it only if it fits on your graphics card next to the chat model, and holds it back while a reply is being written.
vscode.fact4_text: With Easy Link, a message on Telegram or Discord when a long build or command finishes: its name, how long it took and whether it worked, never your code or the terminal output.
vscode.fact5_text: Off by default. The editor’s agents (agent mode of the chat, Cline, Cursor…) can ask a local model, create an image, read a text aloud or proofread it, through MCP, with an access of their own: not your chats, not your settings. ChatonLM’s models can also appear in VS Code’s built-in chat.
vscode.fact6_title: And the rest of the app
vscode.fact6_text: A course about your project or a language in the Study tab, an image generated from a description, proofreading of a file’s comments or of a whole document.
vscode.privacy_text: The extension talks to ChatonLM through a link that never leaves your computer, without going through the network, and only editors paired with a code can use it. With a model on your computer, your code stays on it. If you choose a remote model, the panel tells you before sending, leaves out sensitive files and masks, as best it can, lines that look like secrets. The extension has no telemetry.
vscode.q1: Do I need the ChatonLM app?
vscode.a1: Yes. The extension does nothing on its own: the ChatonLM app, version 0.9.4 or later, runs the models, the voices and speech recognition. Both must be on the same computer, on Windows or Linux.
vscode.q2: Which editors does it work with?
vscode.a2: VS Code 1.105 or later, from the VS Code Marketplace. VSCodium, Cursor and the other editors that install their extensions from Open VSX find it there.
vscode.a3: Not as long as you use a model on your computer: the link between the editor and ChatonLM stays on the machine, and so does the model. Before each request, the panel shows what is sent and whether it stays on this computer. The extension is off in folders you have not marked as trusted.
vscode.a4: A code model made for completion, such as Qwen2.5-Coder. With the Auto setting, ChatonLM picks the size that suits your graphics card, 0.5B, 1.5B or 7B, and offers to download it if it is missing.
vscode.a5: Yes. The extension and the app are free software under the MIT license: no subscription, no credits, no account, no API key to provide.
vscode.end_lead: Install ChatonLM, then the extension. Free, for Windows and Linux.

choose.title: Why ChatonLM, and not another app?
choose.lead: There are plenty of apps for running AI at home, each for one job. ChatonLM brings their tools together in a single app, free and open, and takes care of the details you only notice once you use it: a voice that reads correctly, a conversation that doesn’t overflow, a graphics card you can watch fill up.

r1.else: One app to chat, another to dictate, others to read aloud, to proofread, to create images.
r1.here: Seven tools in a single window, sharing your models and settings.

r2.else: A subscription for each service: the bill soon comes to about sixty euros a month*.
r2.here: Free. No limited trial, no “Pro” version, no credit card.

r3.here: Transcribed on your computer, for dictation and voice mode alike.

r4.else: Often a server to start, a terminal, a container.
r4.here: One installer. The model engine and the image engine are included.

r5.else: A download of several gigabytes, without knowing whether it will fit.
r5.here: Before you download, ModelHub tells you what fits your machine.

r6.here: Windows and Linux, with the same tools.

r7.else: Often closed: you have to take their word for it.
r7.here: Open source, under the MIT license: anyone can read and check it.

choose.details_lead: Three things you can’t see in a screenshot, and notice within the first hour.

voice.title: A voice that reads correctly.
voice.text: A synthetic voice that gets raw text may skip a number, mix up a unit or stumble over an acronym. Before reading an answer aloud, ChatonLM prepares it in its language: numbers, dates, times, units, currencies and version numbers written out in full, acronyms spelled out, formatting and code blocks removed.
voice.proof: The difference is clearest in French and Spanish. On our hardest test sentences in French, misread words were cut by a factor of two to three; in Spanish, without this preparation, the voice lost track of the sentence. And this preparation takes less than a tenth of a millisecond per paragraph: the voice starts no later.
voice.written: Meet on 10/21 at 2:30 pm: the RAM goes up to 32 GB for $15.
voice.spoken: Meet on October twenty-first at two thirty p m: the ram goes up to thirty-two gigabytes for fifteen dollars.

context.title: A conversation that doesn’t overflow.
context.text: A model only remembers a limited number of words: its context. Beyond that, the engine silently forgets the start of the conversation. ChatonLM shows a gauge of the context used; past 80%, it summarizes the oldest messages to make room, and a “Compact now” button does it whenever you like. The whole history stays on screen, and the summary sent to the model is one click away.
context.loops: And if a model starts going in circles, ChatonLM stops it when it repeats itself word for word, or warns you when it keeps rehashing, with a button to stop it.
context.message: So what do you suggest for the rest of the trip?

vram.title: Graphics memory in plain sight.
vram.text: A model that no longer fits on the graphics card spills into system memory and slows down, often without you knowing why. In Settings › Models, a gauge shows each loaded model’s share, other uses and free space, and tells you when part of a model runs from system memory. Unload a model in one click, keep it loaded as long as you like, or preload the one in your chat.
vram.hub: And before you even download, ModelHub tells you whether a model, for text or images, will fit on your card.

choose.q1: Can ChatonLM replace an online AI assistant?
choose.a1: For many uses, yes: chatting, summarizing, proofreading, translating, dictating, studying, creating images. A model that fits on your computer is smaller than those of the big online services and doesn’t match them on everything; in return, it’s free, works offline, and your data stays home.
choose.q2: What does it offer beyond a simple chat interface?
choose.a2: Chat is just one of its seven tools. ChatonLM adds dictation, voice, proofreading, study and image generation, a model catalog that knows your machine, context and graphics memory gauges, and it ships the engine that runs the models.
choose.q3: Do I need to know about local AI?
choose.a3: No. A guided tour shows you the essentials on first launch, ModelHub points you to the models that fit your machine, and everything installs in one click, with no terminal.
choose.q4: Can I keep the models I already have?
choose.a4: Yes. If you used Ollama, or an earlier version of ChatonLM, ChatonLM finds your models and copies them in one click: nothing to download again, and your Ollama stays as it is.
choose.a5: Almost nothing: no account, no telemetry, no ads. The internet is used to browse and download models and voices, to check for updates and, if you turn them on, for web search, remote models and Easy Link. The privacy page details every connection.
